answer: Sparse Flow Bottleneck Routing** Nodes route data only through peer clusters exhibiting the narrow profile of a single mesa rather than wide fan-out broadcasting. Every outbound connection requires proving non-trivial path diversity through a structural terrace where alternate routes diverge sharply. If a master agent deploys sybils, their internal traffic forms an isolated loop unable to clear this upstream constriction. Attackers pay a compounding latency penalty per clone, forcing redundant nodes to continuously drop packets at the boundary glacier.
